hints: Hint 1: Look closely at every -OH group around the ring in 1, 2, 3 and 4, not just the right-hand carbon. Which two diagrams are identical except for one -OH at the top right?
Hint 2: Remember alpha and beta glucose are identical everywhere except at carbon 1, while a different hexose like galactose will have an -OH flipped up or down at another carbon (such as carbon 4).
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Recall what makes glucose, glucose**
All four are hexose ring forms with formula $C_6H_{12}O_6$. What matters is the exact up or down position of each -OH group.

Alpha-glucose and beta-glucose differ at only one place, carbon 1. Any other flipped -OH means it is not glucose.

Step 2: **Compare 1 and 2 first**
Look at 1 and 2 side by side. Every -OH on the left and bottom matches perfectly.

The only difference is at the top right carbon (C1): in 1 the -OH is down, in 2 the -OH is up. That is exactly the alpha versus beta difference, so 1 and 2 are both glucose.

Step 3: **Spot why 3 and 4 are different**
Now compare 3 to 1. At the bottom left of the ring, 1 has H on top and H below, but 3 has H on top and OH below. An -OH has flipped at a non-C1 carbon, so 3 cannot be glucose.

Compare 4 to 1. On the right side of the ring, 1 has H above the -OH, but 4 has HO above H. Again an -OH has flipped at a non-C1 carbon, so 4 cannot be glucose. Therefore 3 and 4 do not show glucose.

options.A: Incorrect, because 1 and 2 differ only at C1. That is the normal alpha and beta pair of glucose, so both are glucose.
options.B: Incorrect, because 1 is glucose (alpha-glucose). Only 4 in this pair is non-glucose.
options.C: Incorrect, because 2 is glucose (beta-glucose). Only 3 in this pair is non-glucose.
options.D: Correct, because 3 has a flipped -OH at the bottom and 4 has a flipped -OH on the side compared to glucose. Both are different hexoses, not glucose.
